title: xdp-sentinel — advanced
description: Advanced DDoS-protection operations view: drop-reason breakdown, attack indicators, rate-limiter effectiveness, protocol/parser detail, host health.

panels.title: Incoming
panels.description: All frames arriving per second.

panels.title: Passed
panels.description: Frames delivered to the machine.

panels.title: Dropped
panels.description: Frames dropped by the dataplane.

panels.title: Drop rate
panels.description: Share of arriving frames dropped.

panels.title: Dataplane
panels.description: XDP program attachment and mode.

panels.title: Feed age
panels.description: Seconds since the agent last exported metrics.

panels.title: Rate-limited
panels.description: Flood packets dropped by the per-source rate limiter.

panels.title: Blocked
panels.description: Packets dropped by a per-source block policy.

panels.title: Bad TCP flags
panels.description: Impossible-flag packets seen (dropped if the flag is on).

panels.title: Malformed
panels.description: Malformed frames (parser errors).

panels.title: Allowlisted
panels.description: Packets passed because the source is allowlisted.

panels.title: Mitigation
panels.description: Active dataplane drop flags (1 = on).

panels.title: Passed vs dropped
panels.description: Stacked; top edge = total arriving. green = passed, red = dropped.

panels.title: Drops by reason
panels.description: Exact breakdown of every dropped packet: rate-limited (flood), blocked (per-source policy), validity (malformed / bad-flags / fragments / UDP filters).

panels.title: Throughput
panels.description: Bit rate of all frames seen by XDP.

panels.title: Drop rate %
panels.description: Share of arriving frames dropped, over time.

panels.title: Connection attempts (SYN/s)
panels.description: New TCP connection attempts per second (SYN without ACK). A sharp climb is a SYN flood.

panels.title: SYN : ACK ratio
panels.description: SYN / (ACK+1). Sustained values >> 1 with high SYN rates = SYN flood (dashed line = 10).

panels.title: Rate limiter: tracked vs limited
panels.description: Packets evaluated by the per-source limiter vs those it dropped. A large limited fraction means active per-source flooding.

panels.title: Transport protocol mix
panels.description: Fully parsed IP packets by transport protocol.

panels.title: TCP flag classes
panels.description: syn / synack / ack / fin / rst per second.

panels.title: Header anomalies / min
panels.description: Anomalous headers per minute (bad flags, LAND, UDP length, IP options).

panels.title: Malformed & unsupported / sec
panels.description: Two always-on lines (sit at 0 when traffic is clean, spike under a bad-packet attack): malformed = RFC-invalid frames (truncated, bad lengths); unsupported = legal but beyond the fast path (deep VLAN/IPv6 stacks). Per-outcome detail is in the xs_parse_outcome_packets_total metric.

panels.title: XDP-seen vs NIC-received
panels.description: Packets counted by XDP vs the kernel's NIC counter; a gap means traffic that bypassed the program (dashed = NIC).

panels.title: Header sampling / sec
panels.description: Headers copied to the sample ring buffer (blue) vs reservations that failed because the collector fell behind (red). Sampling feeds the flow table and per-flow features; both sit at 0 until the 'sampling' config flag is enabled.

panels.title: Sample coverage
panels.description: Share of arriving packets captured as samples (sampled / received). Low coverage under load discounts the confidence of sampled features.

panels.title: L3 protocol mix
panels.description: Frames per second by L3 protocol (valid header).

panels.title: Fragments / sec
panels.description: IPv4/IPv6 fragments (first carries the L4 header, later do not). A fragment flood targets reassembly; drop them with the 'fragments' flag.

panels.title: VLAN tags & IPv6 ext headers / sec
panels.description: Tagged frames (802.1Q / QinQ, by tag count) and IPv6 packets carrying extension headers.

panels.title: Threat state
panels.description: Overall state from the statistical detector (Phase 9): normal / suspect / under attack, computed live from the feature vector.

panels.title: Risk level
panels.description: Mitigation ladder position the risk engine (Phase 13) would apply for the service.

panels.title: Anomaly (robust z)
panels.description: Statistical anomaly score; > 8 marks the window anomalous.

panels.title: DDoS score
panels.description: DDoS classifier (Phase 11) top non-benign probability.

panels.title: Risk & model scores (0-1)
panels.description: Fused risk (red), normalised statistical anomaly, DDoS-classifier score and Isolation-Forest anomaly score over time. All produced by the agent's analysis loop.

panels.title: DDoS classifier — class probabilities
panels.description: Per-attack-type probability from the CART classifier (sums to 1 across classes). The dominant non-benign class names the attack.

panels.title: Auto-mitigation: per-source limit enforced
panels.description: The per-source packets/s ceiling the risk engine applies as it climbs the ladder (lower = more aggressive, 0 = none). The dataplane throttles each flooding source to this rate while normal traffic passes.

panels.title: Mitigation
panels.description: Whether the risk engine is actively blocking/throttling right now.

panels.title: Auto-actions
panels.description: Total mitigation changes the risk engine has applied.

panels.title: Layer 2 — Ethernet
panels.description: ARP floods, non-IP ethertype floods, VLAN abuse.

panels.title: Layer 3 — IP / ICMP
panels.description: ICMP floods, fragment floods, LAND attacks.

panels.title: Layer 4 — TCP / UDP
panels.description: SYN/ACK/RST floods, UDP floods, impossible TCP flags, malformed UDP.

panels.title: Layer 7 — Application
panels.description: HTTP/DNS floods need reverse-proxy or DNS logs (not visible to XDP); stays NORMAL until that source is wired.

panels.title: Active per-layer attacks
panels.description: Which layer and attack type is firing right now (1 = active). L2: arp/ethertype/vlan floods; L3: icmp/frag/land; L4: syn/ack/rst/udp floods, bad flags, malformed UDP.

panels.title: Untracked TCP / sec — ACK/RST flood (conntrack shadow)
panels.description: TCP packets matching no tracked flow: an ACK/RST for a connection that never handshook here. In shadow (conntrack on, drop_untracked off) this is what connection-tracking WOULD drop — it should sit at ~0 for normal traffic and spike under an ACK/RST flood. Enable XS_CONNTRACK_ENFORCE to actually drop it (zero-collateral, after validating this line).

panels.title: Softirq CPU: busiest core vs average
panels.description: XDP/NAPI run in softirq. A core near 100% = packet loss before XDP (generic-mode / single-queue limit).

panels.title: NIC receive drops / errors
panels.description: Packets the host failed to receive (ring full) or received with errors — resource exhaustion before XDP.
